simple.meaning: תְּרָפִים (tᵉrâphîym) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “Teraphim (singular or plural) a family idol.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 15 times across Genesis, Judges, 1 Samuel, 2 Kings, Ezekiel, and 2 more, beginning at Genesis 31:19. Its contexts include family, family line, priesthood, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תְּרָפִים (H8655).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: תְּרָפִים (tᵉrâphîym) / H8655 is traced through Genesis 31:19, Genesis 31:34, Genesis 31:35, Judges 17:5 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: Now Laban had gone to shear his sheep; and Rachel stole the teraphim * teraphim were household idols that may have been associated with inheritance rights to the household property. that were her father’s.
Now Rachel had taken the teraphim, put them in the camel’s saddle, and sat on them. Laban felt around all the tent, but didn’t find them.
She said to her father, “Don’t let my lord be angry that I can’t rise up before you; for I’m having my period.” He searched, but didn’t find the teraphim.

The man Micah had a house of gods, and he made an ephod, and teraphim,* teraphim were household idols that may have been associated with inheritance rights to the household property. and consecrated one of his sons, who became his priest.

Then the five men who went to spy out the country of Laish answered and said to their brothers, “Do you know that there is in these houses an ephod, and teraphim,* teraphim were household idols that may have been associated with inheritance rights to the household property. and a carved image, and a molten image? Now therefore consider what you have to do.”

The five men who went to spy out the land went up, and came in there, and took the engraved image, the ephod, the teraphim, and the molten image; and the priest stood by the entrance of the gate with the six hundred men armed with weapons of war.
When these went into Micah’s house, and took the engraved image, the ephod, the teraphim, and the molten image, the priest said to them, “What are you doing?”
The priest’s heart was glad, and he took the ephod, the teraphim, and the engraved image, and went with the people.

For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as idolatry and teraphim.* teraphim were household idols that may have been associated with inheritance rights to the household property. Because you have rejected Yahweh’s word, he has also rejected you from being king.”

Michal took the teraphim,* teraphim were household idols that may have been associated with inheritance rights to the household property. and laid it in the bed, and put a pillow of goats’ hair at its head, and covered it with clothes.
When the messengers came in, behold, the teraphim was in the bed, with the pillow of goats’ hair at its head.

Moreover Josiah removed those who had familiar spirits, the wizards, and the teraphim,* teraphim were household idols. and the idols, and all the abominations that were seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, that he might confirm the words of the law which were written in the book that Hilkiah the priest found in Yahweh’s house.
the Lord Yahweh says: “Remove the turban, and take off the crown. This will not be as it was. Exalt that which is low, and humble that which is high.
For the children of Israel shall live many days without king, and without prince, and without sacrifice, and without sacred stone, and without ephod or idols.
For the teraphim* teraphim were household idols that may have been associated with inheritance rights to the household property. have spoken vanity,

definitions.short: Teraphim (singular or plural) a family idol
definitions.full: H8655. teraphim תְּרָפִים noun masculine Zech 10:2 plural (= plural of majesty Nö ZMG xlii (1888), 476 ) a kind of idol, object of reverence, and means of divination (√ and etymology-meaning dubious, compare GFM Hast. DB TERAPHIM Say ZA ii. 195 (citing Neubauer, and Assyrian tarpû , spectre ), al. √ רפא , compare רְפָאִים ); — always ׳ת : — portable and sometimes small Gen 31:19 , 34: 31:35 (called אֱלֹהִים 31:30 , all E), but in size and shape like a man 1Sam 19:13 , 16 ; in household shrine (see also l.c.) Judg 17:5 (+ אֵפוֺד , compare GFM Ju ), 18:14 , 17 (both + מַסֵּכָה מֶּסֶל, אֵפוֺד, ), compare 18:20 (omitted מַסֵּכָה ), Hosea 3:4 (+ וֶבַךְ מַצֵּבָה, ׳א, ); condemned 1Sam 15:23 ; 2Kin 23:24 (+ גִּלֻּלִים ); used in divining (by king of Babylonian ), בַּתּ ׳שָׁאַל Ezek 21:26 (+ בַּכָּבֵד רָאָח בַּתִצִּים, קִלְקַל ); as giving empty oracles Zech 10:2 (|| הַקּוֺסְמִים ). — See GFM l.c. Now Archaeology ii. 23 Sta Blb. Theol. d. A. T. under the word . תִּרְצָה see רצה .
